screen: rail wiring across the whole file
finding: The product's primary navigation — the six-tool rail — is prototyped on Settings boards and almost nowhere else. 39 of 45 Settings frames carry rail-wired hotspots; the rest of the file is Media 5/40, Brand 0/34, Layers 0/18, Shell 2/17, Pages 0/13, Journeys 1/74, and ZERO on Insert, Content, Publish, History, Review, AI, Inspector, Compare, Client sign-off, Notifications, Preview, Canvas and Ecommerce.
evidence: Per-module scan of reactions on frames + descendants, carriers named rail/Insert, rail/Layers, rail/Pages, rail/Media. 1090 cross-module edges across 161 distinct pairs; ~409 of them originate in Settings. COUNT CORRECTION (verifier): four of my seven per-module numbers were wrong and all four were too HIGH — Media 5 not 8, Brand 0 not 3, Layers 0 not 2, Pages 0 not 1. Settings 39/45, Shell 2/17, Journeys 1/74 and the thirteen zeros reproduce. The conclusion is strengthened, not weakened: the rail is prototyped even less widely than I said.
recommend: Wire the rail on one representative board per module at minimum, or extract the rail into a single component instance whose reactions travel with it. Until then, anyone walking the prototype can only navigate from Settings, and the file's own edge counts read as 'Settings is the product hub', which it is not.

finding: RETRACTED. I filed Client sign-off as a terminal island because it is the only module with zero outbound cross-module edges. Agent D checked the code: the terminal state is CORRECT BY DESIGN. review-client.tsx:246-249 — 'D · approved, and E · approved but edited since. Both are terminal for the client' — the status!==PENDING branch renders a heading, one paragraph and 'Signed as', zero controls, preview gone. A client who has decided is done. Zero outbound edges is the right shape, not a defect.
evidence: review-client.tsx:246-249 and :287-298. My original evidence (the cross-module matrix) was accurate; the INFERENCE from it was wrong. A module with no exit is only a defect if its user has somewhere to go, and this user does not.
recommend: Two real things survive. (1) Label 1339:7186 'TERMINAL by design' the way its sibling 1339:7193 already is, so the next graph audit does not re-file this. (2) The genuine gap is the AGENCY side, filed by agent D as D-D-18: no review event reaches notifications at all, and notifyReviewSubmitted (review.service.ts:568) filters the requester out of the recipients, so a one-seat agency is told nothing when a client approves.

finding: The raw edge matrix reports Settings/S7 as the file's hub (94 edges to Journeys, 80 to Shell, ~39 to each of Pages/Insert/Layers/Media/Content/Brand). That is an artifact of D-X-01, not an IA fact: the counts are the repeated rail instance on 39 Settings boards.
evidence: 39 of 45 Settings frames are rail-wired vs 0-8 elsewhere; the ~39-40 counts to each rail destination match the rail's six buttons across those boards.
recommend: Recorded so the next reader of the edge matrix does not conclude the product is settings-centred. Any future graph analysis should exclude rail-component reactions or count them once per component, not once per instance.

finding: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED (agent E's D-E-29). The four headline scores on the Preview audit report are painted in the exact hex of the ellipse directly behind them — 91/95/88 are #0e9f6e on a #0e9f6e disc, 72 is #c27803 on #c27803. Contrast 1.00:1. The screen that reports the site's accessibility score fails the check it reports.
evidence: Sibling-shape probe: text fill vs the topmost small shape containing the text centre. 91 text=#0e9f6e behind=#0e9f6e (Ellipse) SAME=true; same for 95, 88; 72 text=#c27803 behind=#c27803. All visible:true, opacity 1.
recommend: White or near-white numerals on the tinted disc. NOTE FOR FUTURE PROBES: my first check compared the text fill to the nearest ANCESTOR with a solid fill and returned bg=#ffffff, same=false — it would have cleared this defect. The disc is a SIBLING, not a parent. An ancestor-walk is the wrong instrument for 'what is behind this text'.

finding: CONFIRMED at the call site (agent F's D-F-31): the copy 'Apply lands as one undo step' is true of the single-message path and FALSE of the multi-step agent run. useAgentRunner.ts:275-287 calls applyAiEdit once per approved step, and applyAiEdit opens exactly one transaction (applySetStyle.ts:642 beginTransaction('ai-edit')). One approve = one transaction = one undo entry, so a three-step run is three. The promise sits directly above the DRAFT row that launches the multi-step run.
evidence: useAgentRunner.ts:275-287 (approve -> applyAiEdit per step); applySetStyle.ts:642 (the single beginTransaction); the copy ships at EmptyThread.tsx:52 and ChatMessage.tsx:65.
recommend: Scope the copy to the path it describes — 'A single edit applies as one undo step; a multi-step run applies one step at a time.' A user leaning on this before pressing Apply on a client's live site is being told the wrong thing in the expensive direction.

finding: The code comment that documents the undo behaviour is itself wrong about the mechanism. AgentPlan.tsx:30-33 says 'each approved step applies in its own transaction (applySetStyle opens one per edit)'. applySetStyle opens NO transaction — applySetStyle.ts:128-133 is just getElement + el.setStyle. The transaction is opened once by applyAiEdit, per approve call.
evidence: applySetStyle.ts:128-133 vs applySetStyle.ts:642. The conclusion the comment draws is right; the reason it gives is not.
recommend: Correct the comment to name applyAiEdit. This is the project's recurring defect class — a comment that outlives the code it describes. Two findings in this same audit were overturned because someone (me, twice) trusted a comment instead of the call site.

finding: CONFIRMED at the call site (agent C's D-C-49). The unsaved-settings dot cannot render on the shipping rail. evidence: LeftSidebar.tsx:105,138,628,638; tabsConfig.ts:349-355. Settings is not on the rail at all — it opens from the site menu — so the prop is dead by construction, not by accident of ordering.

finding: The editor page draws TWO accent blues. #1a56db (the token, --bk-accent) appears on 1355 nodes across 386 boards. #1c64f2 — flowbite blue-600, one step off — appears on 153 nodes across 82 LIVE boards, on nodes named Button and Checkbox, including Components · library/detail/loading/load-error/create and Modal · dirty. DESIGN.md allows one accent.
evidence: Full-page fill sweep of every descendant of every board, blue-ish fills only, then split by whether the parent board's name carries RETIRED/SUPERSEDED/not-implemented/UNBUILDABLE/dashboard-flow. 153 nodes / 82 boards are on live boards; 31 more are on retired or other-scope boards and are excluded. Token value from tokens.generated.css:81. CAUSE FOUND independently by agent I (D-I-04): it is not random drift but a one-step ramp shift. The boards run rest #1C64F2 -> hover #1A56DB; the tokens run rest #1A56DB -> hover #1E429F. The boards' HOVER is the token's REST, so every primary control in the file is drawn one step light on the blue ramp.
recommend: Shift the whole ramp back one step rather than repainting 153 nodes ad hoc: board rest becomes #1A56DB and board hover becomes #1E429F. Agent G measured this on 6 boards, I swept it to 153 across 82 live boards, and agent I explained it — three passes to get one finding right.

finding: NOT A DEFECT, recorded so it is not re-filed. A fill sweep flags 291 rectangles of pure #0000ff across 205 boards with paint alpha 1 — which reads as 291 solid blue blocks drawn on the boards. They are prototyping hotspots at node opacity 0.001.

recommend: No action on the file. The lesson is the instrument: my visibility check tested opacity === 0 exactly, and 0.001 is not 0, so a near-invisible node reported as fully visible. Any future fill sweep must treat opacity below ~0.01 as invisible.

finding: CONFIRMED at the call site, and it is two defects, not one (agent H's D-H-31). review-client.tsx:90-91 renders `{agency}` followed by the literal 'is asking for your feedback'. Line 148 passes agency="Loading", so the loading state of the external client's screen reads "Loading is asking for your feedback". Line 169 passes agency="Buildrick", so the error state reads "Buildrick is asking for your feedback" — and the comment directly above the header says "The agency's name leads, not ours. The client hired them, not us." The error path violates the principle written two lines above it.
evidence: packages/dashboard/app/review/[token]/review-client.tsx:88-92 (header), :148 (Shell agency="Loading"), :169 (Shell agency="Buildrick"), :189 and :253 (the real agency). No canonical board on 1:6 carries this sentence at all; all sixteen S5.5 boards specify 'Reviewing: {Site} · v{n}'.
recommend: Use the board's subtitle. Failing that, a skeleton for the loading state and the real agency name — never a placeholder string — in the error state. This is the one screen in the product seen by someone who is not a user, and it currently introduces the agency as 'Loading'.

finding: The focus ring has FIVE definitions and the root spec is the one being ignored. Page 0:1 Foundations — the file's foundation sheet — states 'FOCUS: 2px accent border/outline, no halo'. a11y.css:99-103 cites that spec BY NAME and obeys it (outline: 2px solid var(--bk-accent); outline-offset: 2px). But tokens.generated.css:203 defines --bk-shadow-focus as a halo (0 0 0 2px rgba(26,86,219,0.30)), buttonTheme.ts:36,40 applies that halo on every button, and all 17 focus variants drawn on page 1:2 use a DROP_SHADOW halo of spread 3. So on a button BOTH apply: an outline the spec asked for and a halo it forbade.
evidence: Screenshotted 481:3979 and read it: 'FOCUS / 2px accent border/outline / no halo'. a11y.css:99 comment quotes the same words. tokens.generated.css:203; buttonTheme.ts:36,40 (tw:focus:ring-0 tw:focus:[box-shadow:var(--bk-shadow-focus)]). Agent I independently found the 17 drawn variants and page 1:2's own rule frame 1034:751, which states a THIRD shape (2px white offset + 2px accent).
recommend: Foundations is the root and the most-repeated interaction state in the product should match it. Either change --bk-shadow-focus to the outline the spec describes, or amend Foundations — but one of the five has to become the source. Note the token is GENERATED from Figma, so fixing it means fixing the Figma variable, not the CSS.

finding: AUDITED, NO ACTION. Page 1:7 is a correctly-maintained archive: 158 of its 159 children carry a supersession marker in their own name, and the one exception is the page's own 'Archived Screens' label. Per the audit's own rule — a board that names its own retirement carries its explanation — none of these is a defect.
evidence: Name scan of all 159 children: 158 match /\[superseded|\[retired|SUPERSEDED|RETIRED/, dated 2026-07-21 (31 with a parseable date) and 2026-08-05 (5). Unmarked: 1 TEXT node, 'Archived Screens'.
recommend: No action. Recorded so this page is not re-audited: it is 159 nodes that would otherwise look like a large unexamined surface.

finding: AUDITED. Two frames: a Foundations sheet (67:2) and 'Elevation · Motion · Z · Focus' (481:3979). The second is a genuine root spec and the product mostly follows it — motion fast 100 / base 160 / slow 240, ease-out cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), 'no springs', which matches DESIGN.md's minimal-motion rule. Its z-scale (canvas 0 · chrome 10 · drawer 20 · topbar 30 · popover 40 · overlay 50 · modal 60 · cmdk 70 · toast 80 · tooltip 90) is a real contract that nothing in this audit has checked against the code.
evidence: Screenshotted and read 481:3979.
recommend: Two follow-ups: the focus rule on this sheet is being ignored by the token and the button theme (D-X-21), and the z-scale deserves a conformance sweep — a modal at the wrong layer is the kind of defect that only shows up when two overlays meet.

finding: The Foundations sheet declares a ten-step z-scale — canvas 0 · chrome 10 · drawer 20 · topbar 30 · popover 40 · overlay 50 · modal 60 · cmdk 70 · toast 80 · tooltip 90 — and the code escalates straight past the top of it. Live values include 10000 (twice), 2000 (twice), 1000 (six times), 301, 300, 199, 100 (three times), plus the tell-tale one-above hacks 91 and 51. Layer order is being decided by escalation, not by the contract.
evidence: Full sweep of z-index in CSS and tw:z-* in TSX across packages/editor/src. Above the scale: TemplatePreviewModal.css 1000, layers-v2.css 1000 x2, Canvas.css 1000 and 100, MediaTab.css 300/301/100, history.css 100, PageTabBar.tsx:471 tw:z-[10000], ImageEditorModal.tsx:306 tw:z-[10000], MediaContextMenu.tsx:137. One-above hacks: PagesTab.css:564 z-index 91 (one over tooltip), LibraryManager.css:457 z-index 51 (one over overlay). On-scale values do exist — 10, 20, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 — so the scale is known and partly used.
recommend: The 91 and 51 are the diagnostic ones: someone hit a stacking conflict and added one rather than asking which layer the element belongs to. Map each off-scale value to its intended tier and replace with the token. Until then two overlays meeting is undefined behaviour — a tooltip at 90 loses to a modal at 1000, and an image editor at 10000 beats everything including the toast that would tell you it failed.

finding: The canvas command palette ships an UNGATED 'Start collaboration session' command. Its handler calls composer.collab.manager.startSession(siteId, 'Editor') directly, with no feature check anywhere in the file. The gate exists and is honoured exactly one place — StudioHeader.tsx:217 reads isFeatureEnabled('collab') for the Collaborate CTA — so this is a bypass of an existing guard, not a missing one. Real-time collaboration is demo-only by founder decision: last-write-wins with six known non-convergence P1 bugs, and CLAUDE.md's env table says of NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_COLLAB, 'Leave off — never in production'.
evidence: editor/canvas/hooks/useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:180-190 — the command object has id/label/category/icon/keywords/handler and no guard; grep for features.collab / isFeatureEnabled("collab") / flags.collab across packages/editor/src returns exactly one hit, StudioHeader.tsx:217. The command is 1 of the 25 the board's own footer counts, and the palette opens on ⌘⇧P for every user.
recommend: Gate the command behind isFeatureEnabled('collab') the way the header CTA is, or drop it from the registry. As it stands a user in production can press ⌘⇧P, type 'collab', and start a multiplayer session on a client's live site — through a feature the founder has said must never ship. The handler also ends in .catch(() => {}), so if it fails the user is told nothing.

finding: CONFIRMED at the schema (agent K's D-K-24), and the risk gradient is INVERTED. theme.push overwrites the brand of every site it touches. Its input makes siteIds OPTIONAL with NO maximum (packages/shared/schemas/theme.ts:22 — z.array(z.string().min(1)).min(1).optional()), and theme.service.ts:151 applies the id filter only when it is present (...(siteIds ? { id: { in: siteIds } } : {})), so omitting it targets EVERY site in the workspace. The service's own comment at :132 says as much. Meanwhile the far safer sites.bulk operation IS capped: packages/shared/schemas/sites.ts:47 is .min(1).max(25). The destructive call is unbounded and defaults to all; the tame one is bounded at 25.
evidence: schemas/theme.ts:22 vs schemas/sites.ts:47; theme.service.ts:132 (comment), :140, :151. Every BrandPush board draws a tidy 4-site selection, so nothing in the design shows the unbounded case.
recommend: Cap theme.push, and make the all-sites case explicit rather than the default of an absent field — an operation that rewrites every client site in a workspace should require naming that it is doing so. The design should draw the unbounded case too; today it only draws four sites.

finding: The type-to-confirm gate has no disabled state, and the board argues for the lock it then fails to draw. 178:512 (empty field) and 179:2 (field typed 'PUSH') are pixel-identical in the action row — the same saturated red Push button at 896,625. The board's own annotation reads 'A checkbox is not enough here — this is the only surface that can damage a site the designer is not looking at.' Filed by agent K as D-K-12; paired here with D-X-28 because they compound: an unbounded destructive call behind a confirm that never appears locked.
evidence: Agent K screenshotted and compared both boards; the action row is identical in position and colour.
recommend: Draw the disabled state, and show which sites are affected — previewSharedThemePush already returns them per site, and the screen names counts (4 sites / 27 pages / 312 elements) without ever naming a site.

finding: CONFIRMED and FIXED (agent J's D-J-16). On page 1:4 the boards were drawn on a 1520px x-step and the captions on their own grid, so 24 of 66 text nodes sat ON TOP of a board — and every sampled one named a DIFFERENT board than the one it covered: 'caption/Domains · none' was drawn over 'Export · format-selected', 'caption/Domains · adding' over 'Export · generating', 'caption/Domains · pending-dns' over 'Export · idle'. A caption sitting on the wrong board does not read as untidy, it reads as a description of that board.
evidence: Overlap probe before: 24 captions intersecting a board, board x-step 1520 vs caption x-step 82. After the layout pass: boards=47, text=66, captions=32, paired=32, unmatched=0, overlaps=0, captions-on-the-wrong-board=0.
recommend: Done, by the same rules used on the editor page: exact normalised name match only, duplicate names dropped rather than guessed. The fix also covers the 34 non-caption text nodes — leaving them out of the first pass left them free to overlap the boards it had just tidied, which is how the defect would have partly returned.

finding: Page 1:5 gridded with the same tool as a preventive pass: 33 boards, 37 text nodes, 27 captions all paired to the board whose name they match, 0 overlaps, 0 captions on the wrong board. Page 0:1 Foundations checked too and needed nothing (2 boards, no captions).

finding: A REFUTATION EXPOSED A PRODUCT BUG.
